newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bunker group to keep Rotterdam in top flight.
newsitem.headline: Bunker group to keep Rotterdam in top flight.

text.p: Bunker players in Rotterdam have formed a working group aimed at maintaining the port's position among the top flight of bunker suppliers with stress on reliability of supply, the port authority said.

"There are no specific problems, but it's a response to the improvements at other ports. We do need to strengthen our position," Tie Schellekens, spokesman for the Rotterdam Municipal Port Management, told Reuters.

The Bunker Monitor Platform Rotterdam, a group of suppliers, refiners, buyers and Dutch authorities, aims to improve the port's service level and to produce a set of self-regulatory principles. It will particularly address quantity and quality issues.
Another body, a grouping of customs, river police and the port authority, has also been established.
"This body will look after measures for the prevention of fraud and short deliveries," the port authority said.
In June 1995, police launched investigations into two bunker trading companies, amid allegations that certain players were undersupplying buyers.
"For the outside, Rotterdam has to be a very reliable port, with no quantity or quality claims. (Certain players) have not always supplied the ordered quantity," one bunker supplier said,
He added that the problem was not unique to Rotterdam.
After Singapore and Fujairah, Rotterdam is the world's third largest bunker port, with annual sales of eight million tonnes.
In 1995, a total of 21,000 bunker transfers were registered at Rotterdam, valued at 1.5 billion guilders, or $900 million, the port authority said.
